message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Year | Key Issue(s) | Main Parties |
|---|--------|------|--------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions between the Latin West and Greek East | Roman Catholic Church (West) vs. Eastern Orthodox Church (East) |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | Authority of Scripture vs. Church tradition, corruption of the clergy, sale of indulgences, theological disputes (e.g., justification by faith) | Roman Catholic Church vs. emerging Protestant denominations (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) |
| 3 | **East–West Schism (Second Great Schism)** | 1965–1970s (often called the “Second East–West Schism”) | Modern theological debates (e.g., ecumenical dialogue, liturgical reforms, social issues), differing interpretations of the role of the papacy and the nature of the sacraments | Roman Catholic Church vs. various Eastern Catholic and Orthodox groups that entered into dialogue or formal separation |

These three events represent the most profound and lasting divisions within Christianity, each reshaping the religious, cultural, and political landscape of their respective eras.
